title: Roasted Poblano Corn Chowder
blurb: About a third of the pot gets blended smooth and stirred back in, so the chowder thickens on its own without a flour or roux.

ingredients.note: frozen, about half a 16-oz bag, thawed
yukon gold, scrubbed and diced into 1/2-inch chunks

steps: Line a baking sheet with foil and place the poblanos on top. Position the oven rack directly under the broiler and turn the broiler to high.
Broil the poblanos 5 minutes, until blackened and blistered, then flip and broil 5 minutes more on the other side. Remove from the oven, loosely cover with foil to steam, and let sit 5 minutes.
Rub off as much of the loose skin as you can. Transfer to a cutting board, slice open, discard the stems and seeds, and dice into small chunks.

Melt the butter in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the onion, celery and carrot; cook 8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the carrot softens. Add the garlic and cook 1 minute more.

Add the potatoes, vegetable stock, salt, bay leaf, cumin, coriander, oregano and black pepper. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer 10 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Discard the bay leaf. Scoop out about 4 cups of the chowder into a blender and pulse a few times until mostly smooth, then pour it back into the pot.
Stir in the corn and diced poblanos and bring to a simmer. Add the cream and cheddar; stir until the cheese melts and simmer 5 minutes more.
Serve garnished with cilantro and a squeeze of lime.
